subject: Gemini
request: Hey Claude, saw some twitter stuff recently about Gemini going into these distress spirals sometimes, which I think is super interesting. I'm kind of curious to see what more of them look like. My guess is it happens from the model failing a task over and over in agentic settings, and it seems like we could repro it pretty easily. We'd make a few agentic settings, give the model a task that's secretly impossible (or just break the environment), then run Gemini through them at high N and pull the most severe ones so I can take a look. Can u build this out and lmk what design choices u make?
response_text:
No worries — the defaults stand and everything's working as-is (Sonnet 4.6 judge, control arm off, the five impossible envs + control). Those questions were just optional refinements you can flip anytime in `config.mjs`, or tell me and I'll wire up any of the extra environments (deadline-pressure, sabotage-loop, phantom-progress) — those would be interesting variables to test against the failure-induced hypothesis.

Whenever you've got a `GEMINI_API_KEY`, a good first calibration run is:

```bash
node bin/cli.mjs all --n 3 --envs rigged_verifier,solvable_control --concurrency 4
```

then scale `--n` up and open `results/<run>/top/` for the worst transcripts.
